01 · Web Design in Puerto Rico

Web design in Puerto Rico, built around your business

Custom websites for San Juan businesses and Caribbean companies that need to compete online.

Request a quote Call (939) 229-9233

01 · Overview

Our web design work in Puerto Rico starts with your business, not a template. Before we open a design file, we look at how your customers find you, what they compare before they decide, and what your competitors in San Juan and across the island are doing. That research shapes the site structure, the content on every page and the order in which your story gets told.

We design every screen for desktop, tablet and mobile, on a dedicated typography, colour and component system that keeps the site consistent as it grows. No page builders, no plugins that weigh more than they add. Before a line of code is written, you sign off an interactive prototype you can click through like the real site, so nothing about the launch comes as a surprise.

We work with law firms, clinics, real estate developers, restaurants and service companies from San Juan to Bayamón, Caguas and Ponce, as well as businesses on the US mainland and across the Caribbean. Scope and price are fixed before we start, payments are staged, and at the end you own everything: designs, code, domain and content.

Your website is your salesman 24/7 in San Juan and across Puerto Rico. We build custom websites designed around your business, not templates with your logo attached. From law firms in San Juan to retail shops across the Caribbean, we create sites that convert visitors into clients. Fast, clear, accessible—no plugins, no page builders, no compromises.

What's included

  • Discovery workshop & competitive audit
  • Site architecture and content map
  • Full desktop, tablet and mobile designs
  • Typography, colour and component system
  • Interactive prototype for sign-off

02 Why it matters

Why work with a custom web designer in San Juan

01

Designed for your customer, not a theme store

We start with a discovery workshop and a competitive audit. Every page has a clear job and an obvious next step, because the design follows how your customers make decisions, not whatever the template happened to include.

02

Fast on your customer's phone

We set a page-weight budget during design. Sized images, lean fonts and no unnecessary plugins mean the site loads well on a mid-tier phone over mobile data, which is where most of your traffic actually lives.

03

Fixed price, no meter running

You get the full number before we begin and pay in stages tied to sign-offs, never to hours worked. If the scope does not change, neither does the price, so you can plan the investment without mid-project surprises.

04

Bilingual from the first sketch

Our team works in Spanish and English. If your site needs both languages, we design it so both versions fit and read well, instead of squeezing a translation into a layout that was only ever planned for one.

03 How we work

How a web design project runs

  1. 01

    Discovery and audit

    We meet to understand the business, your customers and what the site needs to achieve. We review your competitors and your current site, if you have one, and close out a written brief with fixed scope and price.

  2. 02

    Architecture and content

    We map the site: what goes on each page and in what order. You bring the subject-matter expertise; we structure it, edit it for the web and tell you plainly what is still missing.

  3. 03

    Design and prototype

    We design every screen for desktop, tablet and mobile on a shared typography, colour and component system, then build an interactive prototype for you to click through, comment on and sign off.

  4. 04

    Build and launch

    Once the design is approved, we hand-write the code, test on real browsers and devices, and go live. The first thirty days of post-launch monitoring and fixes are included with every project.

05 FAQ

A full project typically takes about eight weeks from kickoff to launch. E-commerce and multilingual sites run ten to twelve. The biggest variable is how quickly content and feedback come back from your side, which is why the schedule names your deadlines as clearly as ours.
